The cassette is angled, showing the top face with the label area and the two spool windows. The internal mechanics (spools) are visible through the transparent plastic casing.

The surface texture is overly grainy and lacks the smooth, specular highlights typical of hard plastic. It looks more like rough paper or stone due to the heavy noise filter/style transfer.
The right-hand edge of the cassette seems to blend slightly into the background without a sharp, defined boundary, suggesting minor geometric ambiguity or melting at the edge.

To verify the physical continuity of the plastic shell and ensure the 'transparent' parts are logically connected to the opaque frame, checking for floating elements.
To ensure the cassette sits firmly on the surface and does not exhibit depth bleeding or impossible perspective warping.
To assess if the grain/noise is an intentional stylistic choice or a degradation artifact affecting structural clarity.
